name: Stout Branch
description: A straight fallen branch thick enough to become a haft, spear shaft, firewood, or frame member.
flavor: "A useful branch is already half a tool."

name: Tannin-Rich Bark
description: Strips of bark rich in tannins, useful for cordage, fire-starting, and preserving hides.
flavor: "The tree gives more than timber."

name: Reed Bundle
description: Long wetland reeds suitable for mats, baskets, thatching, cordage, and kindling.
flavor: "Where the ground is too wet for grass, reeds do the building."

name: Clay Lump
description: Plastic clay dug from damp ground, ready to be shaped and fired.
flavor: "Mud remembers the hands that shaped it."

name: Sharp Stone Flake
description: A deliberately struck stone flake with a keen but fragile edge.
flavor: "The first blade needed no forge."

name: Plant Cordage
description: Twisted plant fibers strong enough for bindings, snares, lashings, and primitive tools.
flavor: "Strength made from many weak fibers."

name: Sinew
description: Cleaned tendon fibers valued for compact, very strong bindings and bow work.
flavor: "Pulled from bone, stronger than it looks."

name: Sinew Cord
description: Tightly twisted sinew cord with excellent tensile strength.
flavor: "It dries hard and holds harder."

name: Rendered Animal Fat
description: Dense animal fat useful for cooking, soap, sealing, and calorie-rich meals.
flavor: "Winter stores itself under the hide."

name: Fresh Offal
description: Nutrient-dense organs that spoil quickly but enrich broths and survival meals.
flavor: "Waste to the careless; strength to the hungry."

name: Fresh Hide
description: Unprocessed hide, heavy with moisture and vulnerable to rot until scraped and preserved.
flavor: "A skin is not leather until work makes it so."

name: Scraped Hide
description: A cleaned hide with flesh and membrane removed, ready for drying or tanning.
flavor: "The blade work shows in every clean patch."

name: Rawhide Sheet
description: A stiff dried hide useful for shields, lashings, containers, and hard-wearing camp gear.
flavor: "Hard as old bark when dry, pliable when soaked."

name: Tanned Leather
description: Flexible preserved hide suitable for clothing, armor, containers, straps, and fine work.
flavor: "Time, bark, water, and patience make skin endure."

name: Flight Feather
description: A stiff flight feather suitable for arrow fletching, bedding, and decorative work.
flavor: "A small piece of the sky left behind."

name: Stone Knife
description: A flaked stone blade lashed to a short handle. Essential for carcass work and hide preparation.
flavor: "Ugly edges still cut cleanly."

name: Stone Pick
description: A heavy stone head bound to a stout branch for breaking softer rock and opening shallow workings.
flavor: "The mountain yields first to persistence, then to metal."

name: Stone Hammer
description: A rounded stone hammer for construction, crushing bone, and rough craft.
flavor: "Simple weight, carefully directed."

name: Digging Stick
description: A fire-hardened stick used to loosen soil, pry roots, and begin primitive farming.
flavor: "The first plow was a branch and stubborn hands."

name: Crude Stone Hoe
description: A broad stone edge lashed to a handle for turning soil more efficiently than a digging stick.
flavor: "A field begins one broken clod at a time."

name: Fire-Hardened Spear
description: A straight branch with a hardened point. Crude, reachy, and far safer than empty hands against game.
flavor: "Keep the teeth at the far end of the shaft."

name: Heavy Club
description: A dense branch trimmed into a brutal close-quarters weapon and pounding tool.
flavor: "No edge to dull, only weight to swing."

name: Fiber Sling
description: A braided sling that turns smooth stones into useful small-game ammunition.
flavor: "A stone travels farther when the cord lends it speed."

name: Sling Stone
description: A smooth palm-sized stone selected for consistent sling flight.
flavor: "The best ammunition is often underfoot."

name: Short Hunting Bow
description: A compact sinew-backed hunting bow suited to woods and close stalking.
flavor: "A bent stave stores patience as force."

name: Stone-Tipped Arrow
description: A light shaft with stone point and feather fletching.
flavor: "Straight wood, sharp stone, steady breath."

name: Bone Awl
description: A polished bone point for piercing leather, bark, and woven material.
flavor: "A little point opens the way for thread."

name: Bone Needle
description: A fine drilled bone needle for stitched leather, cloth, and careful repairs.
flavor: "Small enough to lose, important enough to mourn."

name: Rawhide Buckler
description: A light wooden-and-rawhide hand shield that turns glancing blows aside.
flavor: "Not a wall, just enough between you and the teeth."

name: Fired Clay Cooking Pot
description: A fire-safe clay pot for stews, broths, porridges, boiling water, and rendering fat.
flavor: "A pot turns scattered ingredients into a meal."

name: Wooden Bowl
description: A carved bowl for eating meals, collecting ingredients, and simple camp use.
flavor: "The shape of hunger answered in wood."

name: Small-Game Meat
description: Lean meat from rabbit, hare, or similar small game. Best cooked before eating.
flavor: "Small prey feeds a careful hunter."

name: Red Game Meat
description: Dense red meat from deer, elk, boar, or other large game.
flavor: "A day of tracking condensed into a heavy cut of meat."

name: Raw Poultry
description: Light meat from wild birds, tender but quick to spoil.
flavor: "Feathers on the ground, supper in the pot."

name: Dried Meat
description: Thin strips of meat dried until light, chewy, and resistant to spoilage.
flavor: "Hard travel food that asks only strong teeth."

name: Blueberries
description: Dark wild berries with tart sweetness and useful moisture.
flavor: "A handful stains the fingers and brightens a lean meal."

name: Raspberries
description: Soft red berries that bruise easily and reward careful gathering.
flavor: "Sweet enough that birds always arrive first."

name: Wild Strawberries
description: Small fragrant berries growing close to sunny ground.
flavor: "Tiny fruit with a summer larger than itself."

name: Dandelion Greens
description: Bitter young greens that add fiber and vitamins to soups and stews.
flavor: "The weed survives because it knows the world better than gardeners do."

name: Nettle Leaves
description: Stinging leaves that become edible when cooked and useful as coarse fiber when processed.
flavor: "Handle badly and it bites; handle well and it feeds."

name: Wild Onion
description: Sharp wild bulbs that flavor meals and can yield seed for cultivation.
flavor: "A small bulb with enough scent to announce dinner."

name: Wild Carrot Root
description: A pale tough root, less sweet than cultivated carrot but dependable.
flavor: "Pulled from stubborn ground, still worth the dirt under the nails."

name: Yarrow
description: A pungent flowering herb traditionally valued in field dressings and bitter infusions.
flavor: "White flowers above, old fieldcraft below."

name: Broadleaf Plantain
description: Broad resilient leaves useful in simple poultices and herb mixtures.
flavor: "It grows where boots pass and survives because of it."

name: Morel Mushroom
description: A honeycombed woodland mushroom, valuable cooked and risky to waste.
flavor: "The forest hides good food in shapes that look improbable."

name: Bolete Mushroom
description: A firm woodland mushroom well suited to broths and stews.
flavor: "A quiet cap beneath old trees."

name: Wild Grain Heads
description: Loose heads of wild cereal grain, sparse but enough to seed the first field.
flavor: "Civilization begins when someone saves a handful instead of eating it."

name: Cattail Root
description: A starchy wetland rhizome that becomes much more pleasant after cooking.
flavor: "The marsh keeps its starch underground."

name: Barley Seed
description: Seed saved for planting barley.
flavor: "A future field carried in the palm."

name: Barley
description: Harvested barley suitable for cooking, storage, and seed-saving.
flavor: "A field turns weather and soil into something you can carry."

name: Field Beans Seed
description: Seed saved for planting field beans.
flavor: "A future field carried in the palm."

name: Field Beans
description: Harvested field beans suitable for cooking, storage, and seed-saving.
flavor: "A field turns weather and soil into something you can carry."

name: Cabbage Seed
description: Seed saved for planting cabbage.
flavor: "A future field carried in the palm."

name: Cabbage
description: Harvested cabbage suitable for cooking, storage, and seed-saving.
flavor: "A field turns weather and soil into something you can carry."

name: Carrot Seed
description: Seed saved for planting carrot.
flavor: "A future field carried in the palm."

name: Carrot
description: Harvested carrot suitable for cooking, storage, and seed-saving.
flavor: "A field turns weather and soil into something you can carry."

name: Onion Seed
description: Seed saved for planting onion.
flavor: "A future field carried in the palm."

name: Onion
description: Harvested onion suitable for cooking, storage, and seed-saving.
flavor: "A field turns weather and soil into something you can carry."

name: Flax Seed Seed
description: Seed saved for planting flax seed.
flavor: "A future field carried in the palm."

name: Flax Seed
description: Harvested flax seed suitable for cooking, storage, and seed-saving.
flavor: "A field turns weather and soil into something you can carry."

name: Copper Ore
description: Green- and rust-stained copper-bearing rock from a mineral vein.
flavor: A promising vein mineral whose metal can be worked below iron temperatures.

name: Copper Ingot
description: A cast ingot of refined copper, soft enough for early metalworking.
flavor: Warm red metal carrying the first clear step beyond stone tools.
